sources.note: An Italian proverb benchmark on which models complete proverbs successfully but fail multiple-choice selection when no correct option is present, with CoT analysis showing they name the right ending while failing to notice its absence.
sources.title: Easy to Complete, Hard to Choose: Investigating LLM Performance on the ProverbIT Benchmark

sources.note: A GRPO variant that teaches multimodal models to refuse when a referred object is absent, without losing localization accuracy on cases where it is present.
sources.title: Teaching MLLMs to Say No: Generalized Referring Expression Comprehension via Refusal Calibrated GRPO

result.definition: Declining to answer when no answer is warranted, treated by the sources as a capability separate from answering correctly. In the referring-expression work it is the required output when the described object is absent, and models fail it by emitting hallucinated bounding boxes because training contained no negative samples. In the proverb benchmark it is the harder condition by construction: models complete proverbs successfully but cannot detect that no option is correct, even while naming the right ending in their reasoning. Both sources find abstention degrades independently of task accuracy, so a model can know the answer and still fail to withhold one.
